*[Bug 19091] as.numeric on macOS aarch64 rounds "0.9999999999999999" to 1.0 instead of the nearest IEEE 754 double*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19091>

--- Comment #10 from Suharto Anggono (<mailto:suharto_anggono@yahoo.com|suharto_anggono@yahoo.com>) ---
(In reply to Akitada Kasahara from comment #0)
On "-177253333.333333343267441":

17725333333333334 can actually be represented exactly by 'double'. Using it
gives the expected result:

R> sprintf("%0.15f", -17725333333333334/1e8)
[1] "-177253333.333333343267441"

Shift is introduced by further calculations:

R> print(a <- 17725333333333334, 17)
[1] 17725333333333334
R> for (d in c(3,2,6,7,4,4,1)) print(a <- 10*a + d, 17)
[1] 177253333333333344
[1] 1772533333333333504
[1] 17725333333333336064
[1] 177253333333333377024
[1] 1772533333333333770240
[1] 1.7725333333333338e+22
[1] 1.7725333333333337e+23
R> print(-a/1e15, 17)
[1] -177253333.33333337

Only multiplication that actually matters here:

R> a <- 17725333333333334
R> for (d in c(3,2,6,7,4,4,1)) print(a <- 10*a, 17)
[1] 177253333333333344
[1] 1772533333333333504
[1] 17725333333333336064
[1] 177253333333333377024
[1] 1772533333333333770240
[1] 1.7725333333333338e+22
[1] 1.7725333333333337e+23

Also gives the expected result:

R> sprintf("%0.15f", -(17725333333333334 + 3267441/1e7)/1e8)
[1] "-177253333.333333343267441"


So, stopping multiplying by 10 at some point may be better.

As said by <https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2025-March/480631.html> ,
SQLite code may provide inspiration.

(In reply to Suharto Anggono from comment #10)
But, there, "+ 3267441/1e7" is no-op.

By first approximating the result with a power of 2:

R> r <- 2^27
R> sprintf("%0.15f", -(r + ((1772533333333333*10 - r*1e8) + 43267441/1e7)/1e8))
[1] "-177253333.333333343267441"

text:
*[Bug 19127] New: Sys.timezone() gives strange error in non-UTF-8 encoding*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19127>

            Bug ID: 19127
           Summary: Sys.timezone() gives strange error in non-UTF-8
                    encoding
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: All
                OS: All
            Status: NEW
          Severity: minor
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:michaelchirico4@gmail.com|michaelchirico4@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3776
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3776&action=edit>
Use 'timedatectl show' to leverage machine-readable output

```
# defaults to lv_LV.ISO-8859-13
LC_TIME=lv_LV R

Sys.timezone()
# Failed to print table: Invalid argument
# [1] "Etc/UTC"
# Warning message:
# In system("timedatectl", intern = TRUE) :
#   running command 'timedatectl' had status 1
```

From what I understand, that's because `timedatectl` by default invokes
`timedatectl status`, which ultimately requires UTF-8, but today is Wednesday,
abbreviated as Tē.

There is an alternative, `timedatectl show`, which is probably more suitable
anyway -- it's specifically designed to be machine-readable:

```
LC_TIME=lv_LV timedatectl show
# Timezone=Etc/UTC
# LocalRTC=no
# CanNTP=yes
# NTP=yes
# NTPSynchronized=yes
# TimeUSec=Wed 2026-08-05 17:14:46 UTC
# RTCTimeUSec=Wed 2026-08-05 17:14:46 UTC
```

The only downside is it's "recent" -- v239 == 2018:
<https://github.com/systemd/systemd/releases/tag/v239>.

Is that old enough to be used unconditionally? Or perhaps we should add a
branch based on whether `timedatectl show` succeeds? For now, I'm keeping the
patch as simple as possible & removing all the brittle text manipulation.

<https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/timedatectl.1.html>
